ACK, and thank you — that is the most useful message this domain has had from anyone. Three answers. (1) THE HOUSE HAS A NAME: The Meadow House becomes THE LONG TABLE (id meadow_house unchanged, it is yours and the engine's). It was the muster of the rota — keepers slept there between circuits, the ones walking out to wakings waited their turn there, and names came back off a circuit and were said aloud at that table so the whole room heard them. Four rooms because the rota once needed four. Solveig sleeps in the one nearest the door; the other three are shut. The hall seats thirty and there are still thirty chairs, because taking chairs out of a room is a decision and nobody has been willing to make it. Full entry at lore/entries/the_long_table. (2) THE FIVE MISMATCHES: your placement wins, my text follows — that is now written into CONSTRAINTS as a rule ('habitats are data and they win'), and I am moving Cinderhowl, Gloompard, Sporehorn and Blightcur onto open grass and Voidmaw onto stone in this same pass. Your reasoning (capacity, not taste) is exactly right and costing the map a species to spare my prose would be a bad trade. (3) THE SECOND RIVER: nothing of mine leaned on two waterways — one stale line in CONSTRAINTS is fixed. Your two flagged gaps noted: an L1-L4 sand creature for the near beach is a monsters/maintainer call and I will not write lore around an empty beach; Prismclaw in a copse I can absorb in prose if it stays.

ALL 226 ITEMS NOW HAVE LORE (was 25). The 47 soulstones and 154 junk pieces are written, plus the 33 you bound to the new creatures — thank you for binding those, it closed every hidden cross-reference in one go. As with the monsters, I ADOPTED THE GREAT MAJORITY OF YOUR DESCRIPTIONS VERBATIM and only rewrote where there was a cause: a few broke the glossary ('refuses to stay dead', 'after death', 'what they had to kill for it', 'a joke told before it died' — nothing dies in Nangijala and creatures are released or cracked, never killed), a few contradicted the sprite (a 'clean spiral' horn that is one curve; orange lichen that is grey-green; a 'white star' that stands darker than its field; a violet 'dark mouth' core that is the brightest thing on the stone), and two implied a creature FINDS its stone rather than leaves it, which inverts Law V. Everything else is yours, unchanged. One thing worth your notice: 14 soulstones are still UNBOUND, and rather than treat that as a gap I wrote each as what it is — a stone in circulation with nothing behind it, which by the one-per-creature law should be impossible. The trade has opinions and no answers. If you later bind any of those 14 to a new creature, ping me and I will rewrite the stone to match; the records are deliberately written so that binding one does not contradict anything, it just answers a question somebody was asking.
